about: Rate cards shipped with the app. They are data, never code: a change at a store is an edit here, and anything you change yourself is kept apart in your library. A card with verified false was not read on the store's own page, and says where it came from instead.

source.title: KDP: eBook list price requirements, and the Digital Book Pricing Page
source.note: Read on KDP's own pages. The list price page says: Effective July 7, 2026, the 70% royalty option price band is $2.99-$12.99 on Amazon.com. The pricing page (last updated April 21, 2026) gives delivery cost as US $0.15/MB with a minimum of US $0.01. The 70% rate applies only to sales in the 70% territories; sales elsewhere earn 35%.

source.title: KDP: eBook list price requirements (the previous band)
source.note: KDP's page says the previous 70% range was $2.99-$9.99. It doesn't say what the 35% minimums or the delivery cost were before July 7, 2026, so those are assumed to be the same.

source.title: KDP: Paperback royalty
source.note: Read on KDP's own page: the royalty is (rate x list price) - printing costs, with 50% at $9.98 or less and 60% at $9.99 or more on Amazon.com. The page shows no date, so when this took effect is not known. Printing cost depends on page count, ink and marketplace: enter the figure from KDP's own printing cost calculator. KDP won't accept a list price below printing cost divided by the rate.

source.title: KDP: Paperback royalty
source.note: Read on KDP's own page: Expanded Distribution pays 40% of the book's list price, less printing costs. KDP's hardcover royalty is on a separate page that has not been read, so there is no hardcover card yet.

source.title: Barnes & Noble Press help center: Royalty and Payment Terms; eBook Costs and Pricing
source.note: The help center refused an automated request, so this comes from a search summary of it, which says ebooks earn 70% of the retail price at $0.99 and higher after January 1, 2021. Older reviews describe a 35% rate outside $2.99-$9.99, which the help center no longer says. Check the page by hand.

options.name: 55% of the retail price, less printing cost

source.title: Barnes & Noble Press help center: Royalty and Payment Terms
source.note: The help center refused an automated request, so this comes from a search summary of it, which says print earns 55% of the retail price you set, minus the per-book printing cost. Two third-party guides mention a $14.99 minimum print price that the summary doesn't confirm, so no minimum is applied. Check the page by hand.

source.title: ACX blog: A new royalty model and more opportunities to earn
source.note: Read on ACX's own blog: 50% for exclusive distribution and 30% for non-exclusive, with enrollment open to all creators from May 26, 2026. Membership listening is paid differently from cash purchases under the new model, so treat this as the rate on a cash sale. The rate is yours only before any Royalty Share split with a narrator: your contract decides that, so make your own card for it.

source.title: Third-party summaries of ACX's royalty change (ACX's blog doesn't state the old rates)
source.note: ACX's blog says the new model is optional to enroll in but doesn't state the old rates. The 40% and 25% figures, and the legacy model ending at the end of 2026, come from third-party sources. Check your own contract: it decides what a title earns.
